name_en: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
canonical_claim: For every positive modulus and every residue class coprime to that modulus, there are infinitely many prime natural numbers in that residue class.
domain_and_universes: q : Nat with [NeZero q]; a : ZMod q with IsUnit a; p : Nat. The q = 1 boundary is included and q = 0 is excluded.
quantifiers: IsUnit a implies infinitude of natural primes reducing to a
conclusion: The primes congruent to a modulo q form an infinite set; equivalently, above every natural bound there is such a prime.

alternate_encodings.target: infinitude of the set of primes in the residue class
for every bound n there exists a prime p > n in the residue class

excluded_degenerate_cases: q = 0 and nonunit residue classes are excluded by explicit hypotheses. q = 1 is included. Primality is over Nat, not Int.
